Wontfix.

The bead is correctly self-labeled 'opinion' and self-acknowledges 'the current shape IS boring and readable; the smell is the maintenance compound, not legibility per block.'

Workspace AGENTS.md 'Scope and Style' rule: 'Keep solutions simple and direct; prefer boring, readable code.' Each of the 8 sequential 'if x == 0 { return Err(...) }' blocks is independently readable, the error message is colocated with the field name, and a reader following a clippy report or a fuzzing failure can jump straight to the right block.

Extracting a check_nonzero_<T> helper trades 8 boring lines for 4 lines of helper + 8 call-sites, with one indirection added between the field check and the error text. Net legibility wins are negligible; the 'easier to extend when the 9th field arrives' argument is real but small — extending the boring shape adds one boring block, and that has not been a maintenance burden historically.

Closing per workspace AGENTS.md anti-bikeshedding policy: 'If you are out of real issues to flag, say so. Do not manufacture problems to fill space.' bd:JMAP-6r7c.51.
description: crate-jmap-base-client/src/client.rs:108-146 ClientConfig::validate hand-rolls seven near-identical 'if self.<field> == 0 { return Err(ClientError::InvalidArgument(format!("ClientConfig.<field> must be > 0"))); }' blocks plus one Duration::ZERO variant. The repetition is mechanical: each block differs only in field name and the field's friendly name embedded in the error string. Idiomatic Rust collapses this either via a tiny check-helper that takes (field-value, field-name) and returns Result<(), ClientError>, or — more aligned with this crate's style of pre-validating at construction — via a single match over a fixed list of (field, condition) tuples that emits the first failure. Neither is dramatic, both are easier to extend when the ninth field arrives (it always does). The 8 == 0 checks today expand to the 9th, 10th, 11th sequentially as new ClientConfig fields are added per the cookie-cutter pattern. Recommendation: extract a check_nonzero_<T> helper per type (Duration, usize, u64) — three helpers — and call site shrinks to one line each. Defended against by: workspace AGENTS.md prefers boring readable code, and the current shape IS boring and readable; the smell is the maintenance compound, not legibility per block.
title: ClientConfig::validate is 8 sequential 'if x == 0 { return Err(...) }' blocks — repetition smell
